themes_detail.label: Illegal Posting Surge
themes_detail.summary: Illegal posting complaints spiked to 3 THIS WEEK versus a baseline average of 0.1 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 2300% increase—suggesting a coordinated posting campaign or sudden enforcement gap in CD309.
evidence: 3 illegal posting complaints THIS WEEK vs 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 8.69)
2300% spike represents most acute one-week acceleration in district complaint data
No prior precedent for this volume in baseline period suggests new activity pattern
reporting_angles: Ground-truth: Are specific blocks being targeted? Interview sanitation and local business owners about what they're seeing.
Enforcement angle: Has the city's illegal posting response team been deployed to Flatbush/PLG, or is this a resource gap?

themes_detail.label: Public Drinking & Park Rule Violations
themes_detail.summary: Public drinking complaints hit 7 THIS WEEK (367% above the 1.5 weekly baseline) and park rule violations reached 4 THIS WEEK (967% above 0.4 baseline), together suggesting concentrated disorder in a specific park or public space.
evidence: 7 drinking complaints THIS WEEK vs 1.5 weekly average (z-score: 7.78)
4 park rule violations THIS WEEK vs 0.4 weekly average (z-score: 7.49)
Combined signal suggests concentration in 1-2 locations rather than district-wide diffusion
reporting_angles: Localization: Map the complaints—are they clustered at Prospect Park, Parade Grounds, or another specific venue? Interview Parks enforcement and local precinct.
Root cause: Have there been reductions in Parks patrol, or has a new encampment formed? Talk to CBOs working on homelessness (CB budget requests mention DHS capital requests repeatedly).

themes_detail.label: Construction Complaints Spike
themes_detail.summary: General construction and plumbing complaints surged to 65 THIS WEEK versus a baseline of 13.4 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 386% increase—coinciding with 351 DOB permits filed in the last 90 days, suggesting inadequate enforcement or a cluster of unruly projects.
evidence: 65 construction/plumbing complaints THIS WEEK vs 13.4 weekly average (z-score: 7.14)
351 DOB permit filings in last 90 days (221 alterations, 76 new buildings) provide context for complaint surge
Suggests either enforcement gap at HPD/DOB or overlap of multiple active projects in same micro-neighborhoods
reporting_angles: Permit audit: Which 5-10 projects are generating the most complaints? Interview DOB about enforcement frequency and penalties.
Resident impact: Are noise/dust violations concentrated in residential blocks? Talk to affected tenants and tenant associations.

themes_detail.label: Graffiti Wave (3 weeks ago)
themes_detail.summary: Graffiti complaints peaked at 102 THREE WEEKS AGO, representing a 2231% spike from the 4.4 weekly baseline (z-score: 14.4, highest statistical anomaly), though this may have subsided; requires current verification to assess whether it was a one-time surge or ongoing problem.
evidence: 102 graffiti complaints 3 weeks ago vs 4.4 weekly average (z-score: 14.4, highest z-score in dataset)
2231% spike is most extreme statistical anomaly in all complaint categories
No follow-up spike data provided; unclear if problem persists or resolved
reporting_angles: Follow-up check: Are graffiti levels still elevated, or did the spike resolve? Ground-truth by photographing hotspots.
Root cause investigation: Was this a coordinated tagging campaign, a gang activity marker, or a response to removal delays? Talk to NYPD gang units and graffiti removal contractors.

themes_detail.label: Consumer Complaint Uptick
themes_detail.summary: Consumer complaints jumped to 7 LAST WEEK versus a 1.5 weekly baseline—a 367% increase (z-score: 7.78)—but the nature and clustering of these complaints are unclear; requires specificity to determine if this reflects a single bad actor or systemic issue.
evidence: 7 consumer complaints last week vs 1.5 weekly average (z-score: 7.78)
367% spike shows statistical significance but lacks categorical detail in available data
Requires deeper dive into complaint type (food safety, retail fraud, etc.) to assess newsworthiness
reporting_angles: Data drill-down: Obtain 311 complaint detail—are these food establishments, retail, unlicensed services? One bad actor or multiple?
If food-related: Partner with health dept on any pending inspections in Flatbush/PLG to contextualize.
